edits.marker: ## Retained consequence can exceed current evaluative use
edits.addition:
## Correction can use an interaction omitted from the schedule

The [context-sensitive correction study](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONTEXT-SENSITIVE-CORRECTION-INTEGRATION.md) returns to the existing relay history. Three saved cases have identical controller/account records despite different actual outcomes: ordinary success, a weak-to-full calibration failure and a false contact reporting dependence where the weak response is absent. The retained evidence alone cannot distinguish these histories. The original controller also acquires no final full-load receipt.

Closer reconstruction reveals an operation that this record omits. The existing event law allows the pending on-setting response to pass through contact zero while preserving its actual setting tag. The old executor always uses the matching contact index, so it never requests that alternative. Six continuations through the unchanged methods, independently checked across 42 transitions, show that the alternate contact corrects the false acquired bit and changes the existing reader's selection. Earlier sensory knowledge, completion, source stocks and the original account remain intact. The ordinary-contact controls keep the original ambiguity.

This corrects the research trajectory: absence from a represented schedule is not absence from the generative process represented by its broader law. The branch can therefore revise the core's articulation and the analyst's description together. Sensing, record formation, selection and action remain differentiated activities within the history; their distinction does not make them fundamentally independent.

The source interface supplies selectable contact semantics and channel-zero faithfulness. These runs neither form a physical route nor teach the original executor to choose the inquiry. Ordinary success and calibration failure still produce the same new record; both weak relations are genuinely the same. Acquiring the full-operation effect and revising its application remain specific interfaces. No new source packet or successful repair is created, and unique fault diagnosis is unnecessary whenever one adequate continuation serves the remaining possibilities. Existing acquired-criterion and inquiry-sufficiency results retain their scope. The next explanation follows actual consequences into a warranted choice and use of an available inquiry, rather than adding a reader for a distinction the existing law can already acquire.
